title: Act I: Touchdown at Hadley-Apennine & Standup EVA

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Descent engine throttle down to 10 percent... 100 feet, descending slowly. Jim, watch that dust kicking up below the footpads.

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: Altitude 40 feet, coming down at two feet per second. Surface visibility is getting hazy with the blowback, Dave. Pitch looks clean. Thirty feet.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Shutdown! Aerozine 50 and oxidizer valves closed. Falcon has touched down.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Houston, <color=#00FFFF>Falcon is on the Plain at Hadley.</color>

lines.speaker: Joe Allen (CAPCOM)
lines.text: Roger, Falcon. We copy you down at Hadley-Apennine! Breath of fresh air here in Mission Control. You're looking magnificent.

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: Look at those mountains out the triangular window, Dave! Mount Hadley rises straight up over four thousand meters above us. Not a drop of haze.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: It's breathtaking. Because there's no atmosphere to scatter the sunlight, distances are completely deceiving. Those towering peaks look like you could reach out and touch them.

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: Telemetry shows landing site coordinates around 26.13 degrees North, 3.63 degrees East in the Mare Imbrium basin. We tilted slightly on a crater slope, but Falcon's four gear legs are solid.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Cabin pressure dumped. Suits locked. I'm opening the upper docking hatch for our Standup EVA. Time for our initial 360-degree photographic survey.

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: I have your umbilical cables supported, Dave. Telephoto 500-millimeter lens is ready to pass up to you.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Oh, what a sight! Looking south toward Saint George Crater and the Swann Range. The rim of Hadley Rille is clearly visible to the west—a dramatic chasm cutting through the lava plain.

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: Any huge boulders blocking our driving routes for tomorrow?

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Negative, Jim. The undulating mare is cratered, but the slopes are rounded. Our Lunar Roving Vehicle should navigate this terrain smoothly.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Standup survey complete after 33 minutes. Hatch secured and cabin repressurized. Let's prep for our full EVA-1 egress tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: Fast forward to EVA-1 morning: backpacks pressurized, cabin vented. Hatch is open, Dave. The porch and ladder are all yours.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Backing out the hatch onto the platform... down the nine ladder rungs. Stepping onto the footpad.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: "As I stand out here in the wonders of the Unknown at Hadley, I realize there's a fundamental truth to our nature. Man must explore. And this is exploration at its greatest."

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: Amen to that, Dave. Coming down behind you. The boots sink only an inch or two into this fine powder. Let's inspect Falcon's descent stage and get to work.
